findings.passage: What keeps the Nine ahead is narrower: what she asks for. When she objected at the time, in 2021 and 2023, she did not name a danger or a person she could not trust.
findings.problem: The one separator left between Type 9 and Type 6 does not hold against the page's own sources. (1) A dated 2021 objection names fear: on January 19, 2021 she wrote 'I'm not comfortable making TikToks anymore' and explained 'i have a lot of fear in me' (Complex), an exhibit the page prints two paragraphs earlier. (2) 'I want to be home' is cut from 'I want to be home. I want to make music. I want to play video games,' and Capital FM and Rolling Stone both report that Live as wanting time to make music, which is her own agenda and not rest. (3) The October 2021 tweets are an exhaustion statement ('im never not working. im fucking tired'); a tired Six would also ask for rest, which the evidence record concedes and the page does not say. (4) The island line is a taunt inside an album-title announcement. (5) Asrat's line is a counterfactual about cooking, and Lewis's 'she just comes in, and she's so relaxed' describes how easily she writes songs, not a resting state. (6) 'She does ask for that, but later' leaves out her own account of an earlier reassurance habit ('I need tarot cards. I need an answer. Text me,' Vogue 2026, held in the record). The warrant about what a Six asks for is unsourced. With order and reason already conceded on the page, no defensible discriminator remains.
findings.acceptance_test: Research produces a discriminator that Type 6 fails on dated, sourced evidence and that survives a full table of her on-record objections, including January 2021; or the evidence status moves to insufficient_evidence and the page stays held under the owner note, with no switch to Six and no return to Seven. Wherever the page says what she asked for, it prints the January 2021 statement and the full November 2021 quotation, describes the Asrat and Lewis lines as what they are, and weighs 'I need an answer. Text me' beside 'but later.'

findings.passage: So the swing from blowup to "I'm fine" is not credited to type here. The lean rests on what is left: the yes itself, what she asked for, and what others saw.

research_tasks: Build a dated table of every on-record objection from 2019 to 2026 (the January 2021 TikTok withdrawal, October and November 2021, Paraguay in March 2022, May 2023, Threads in July 2023, the March 2024 Instagram exit, June 2025, Auckland in November 2025) with the reason she gave and what she asked for, each from an opened source. Test any Nine-over-Six separator against the whole table, including the statements that name fear.

Find first-hand, dated testimony about how she behaves off-cycle from people who do not work for her (SZA, Jack Antonoff, friends, family): with nothing scheduled, does she rest and drift, or prepare and seek reassurance? The only outside observations on the page are a manager's remark about cooking and an engineer's about songwriting.

Date the reassurance habit she describes as pre-therapy ('I need tarot cards. I need an answer. Text me,' Vogue, March 2026) and look for contemporaneous evidence of it, or of its absence, before 2024. The page's 'She does ask for that, but later' depends on it.

Open her TikTok of 2026-03-13 first-hand (and those of 2026-03-20 and 2026-08-31) for her full wording on 'pretend that I like stuff.' Whether she ties it to agreeing to obligations decides whether 'the yes itself' can be used as type evidence at all.
Open the New York Times interview published 2025-09-05 directly; the page relies on Revolt's relay for 'I want to return back to what I know.'

Verify and date the two leads the fan reviewer raised from general knowledge: the July 2022 Noah Schnapp direct-message episode (an immediate public no) and the 2022 Taco Bell TikTok in which she called the jingle contractual (going along while saying so).
